researchUpdates.title: Quantitative Assessment of Precursor Crystallinity on the Reactivity and Strength of Basalt-Based Geopolymers
researchUpdates.authors: Haifeng Pang, Jifeng Wu, Tong Shi, Chunming Hou, Xiongfei Wu, Zibo Yan and Miao Deng
researchUpdates.summary: Controlled heat treatment of basalt glass links increasing crystallinity with reduced reactivity and compressive performance.
highlights: Uses related glass precursors to examine mineral structure while limiting chemical-composition differences.
The fitted strength relationship describes this dataset; it is not a validated predictor for other binders.
researchUpdates.summaryBasis: Indexed primary publisher text, including abstract and selected methods/discussion; direct page returned HTTP 429; no full methods audit
researchUpdates.access: Crystallinity is semi-quantitative. The plotted zero-strength endpoint is a theoretical failure boundary, not a measured compression result. No independent replication or age-based prediction established.

researchUpdates.title: Investigation of coal mine overburden as a sustainable fine aggregate in alkali-activated concrete
researchUpdates.authors: Sanchita Nawale and Rahul V. Ralegaonkar
researchUpdates.summary: Coal-mine overburden replaces natural fine aggregate in a one-part fly ash/slag concrete activated with powdered sodium metasilicate.
highlights: The selected all-overburden fine-aggregate mixture reached a reported 48.99 MPa in compression at 28 days.
The study also evaluates other mechanical properties and estimates energy and cost within a defined comparison.
researchUpdates.summaryBasis: Primary publisher abstract, metadata and selected introductory methods; full methods not audited
researchUpdates.access: Source-specific laboratory results. Energy and cost estimates depend on local inputs and assessment boundaries; no general environmental qualification or independent replication. Compression is not shear, flexure or bond.

journalArticle.title: Material history belongs beside the mix proportions
journalArticle.summary: Two new studies show why a formulation database needs mineral structure and aggregate provenance alongside ingredient weights.
paragraphs: Pang and colleagues vary the crystallinity of basalt-derived precursors and report changes in compressive performance. Their fitted relationship remains specific to the tested system; even the plotted zero-strength endpoint represents a failure boundary rather than a measured load.

Nawale and Ralegaonkar investigate coal-mine overburden as fine aggregate in a one-part binder. Their findings concern a particular waste source and formulation, with energy and cost comparisons bounded by the study assumptions.

Our editorial takeaway for the recipe database is to record material source, processing history and characterization alongside proportions. A future advisor should distinguish measured results from fitted estimates and ask for missing material information before suggesting a comparison. These studies do not validate user recipes or supply unreported strength timelines.
